The card's premise holds and is delivered, but all three of its mechanical assumptions were falsified by measurement and each changed the design. (1) The title convention is followed by NOTHING: the documented form in .claude/skills/checklist-test/SKILL.md and the form described in the card are both 0/23; 23/23 records use a fifth shape with judged/total folded into a parenthetical on the selector in five distinct phrasings, absent entirely on one. (2) The per-item verdict tables do not have one shape and are deliberately NOT parsed: 9 of 23 records carry no markdown table at all, the other 14 carry 26 distinct header shapes, and most are clause-level rather than item-level -- they use the word 'verdict' for a different unit, so counting them would yield a confidently wrong matrix. The script reads the title counts (the only uniform machine-readable field, authored by the runner) and states in every run that it did not read the bodies. (3) Staleness had to become three-valued: this container is a shallow clone (boundary 713ccbc95, 2026-08-16) and the 92f26f75 wave predates it, so merge-base --is-ancestor answers false for commits that are almost certainly ancestors -- a boolean would have rendered the NINE STALEST RECORDS AS FRESH. 'Could not tell' renders as ? with its reason and is never counted as fresh. Corpus is 23 records, not the 14 the card assumed. No root package.json entry: scope discipline, and the file is held by two open PRs (see open_questions for the factual conflict finding).",

The self-test caught two real defects during development, both fixed: a date validator that accepted 2026-13-99 (the date is the latest-wins sort key, so an impossible date had to become unparseable rather than silently order the roll-up), and a placeholder GH_TOKEN being forwarded as a Bearer header, which produced a 401 that reads as 'no access' when access was fine. LIVE RUN against the real corpus: 23 records, 23 parsed, 0 unparseable, 0 open, 1 REST call.
